summary.description: Cadmium is a soft silvery metal naturally found in minerals and commonly used in batteries, coatings, pigments, plastics, and low-melting alloys.
emission_sources: Metal processing (e.g. zinc, aluminium, iron and steel)
Combustion of fossil fuels in power stations
environmental_impact: Bioaccumulation in organisms such as micro-organisms and molluscs
Toxic effects on plant and animal growth and reproduction after prolonged exposure

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Cadmium is toxic to humans, particularly with long-term exposure, leading to health issues through contaminated food and water sources.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Cadmium bioaccumulates in aquatic organisms and disrupts marine ecosystems, particularly affecting reproduction and survival of species like molluscs.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Cadmium pollution results from inadequate waste management, especially in battery recycling and metal production, requiring improved production and disposal practices.
